transcript: The other night, I saw Swept Away on Broadway. In a nutshell, I’d describe this new musical as “men harmonizing against a dark and stormy backdrop of a plot” — it's basically about four guys trying to survive after a shipwreck. I liked it but I didn't love it. My biggest gripe was that even at just 95 minutes, it felt like this plot was struggling to fill that 95 minutes. About half the show goes by before the shipwreck even happens, and the exposition in that first half isn't very necessary for the real meat of the show in the second half. But it does give the opportunity for the ensemble to shine before the masterful shipwreck scene which I won't spoil any further. With the exception of Stark Sands, I kind of felt like the cast was giving pretty generic vocals, but I think the monotonous score contributes to this. The music, which is preexisting songs by the Avett Brothers, is pleasant and well performed, but I felt like there wasn't enough sonic variation throughout the show and the songs didn't really advance the plot — and this is what made it very obvious to me that it was a jukebox musical. On the flip side, much of the acting, particularly from John Gallagher Jr, was great and I think in a more intimate venue the story would have hit even harder. Overall, I would say the main draw here is if you're into the kind of music that the show offers, and otherwise it's not a must see. With that, another playbill for my collection.
